query: A report says the Netherlands's government borrowing at 5.5% in 2013 carried an effective cost of 5.8% once the rise in the price of the economy's total output (not consumer prices) is taken out. Is that right?

text.text: Identifies that the real interest rate is the nominal rate deflated by inflation, r=(1+i)/(1+pi)-1 with pi the GDP deflator change.
text.accept: names the accepted approach; alternative: report both deflator-based and note CPI-based as a variant; gold uses GDP deflator

data.text: Uses WEO nominal GDP and GDP deflator series (NGDP_D, (nominal rate stated in query)).

computation.text: Real rate NLD 2013 i=5.5% = 4.30 %; statement 5.8% is outside tolerance
Verdict: statement is FALSE under the recomputed value.

assembled_from: Escolano (2010) A Practical Guide to Public Debt Dynamics (doc 55319ff9-c45c-4e8d-99e4-5562a1158bf2)
provenance.selection: seeded draw over top-20 economies by 2024 USD GDP (frozen), one per country-year

gold_report_note: Published value is WEO series or none; no corpus report states it, nothing to withhold.
